purpose: Define a falsifiable Candidate Enterprise Posture (CEP) and the minimum semantic runtime slice lattice required to move ICTC from the current market-candidate runtime plus separate enterprise benchmark kernel to one enterprise-mountable product runtime without laundering repository evidence into production readiness.

cepDefinition.name: Candidate Enterprise Posture
cepDefinition.positiveClaim: On one exact repository head, ICTC exposes the same seven-procedure business and epistemic semantics through a canonical runtime contract that can be mounted in an enterprise deployment mode backed by shared durable authorities, with fail-closed identity, tenant, concurrency, evidence, AI, observability and delivery boundaries and with executable repository evidence for the declared candidate envelope.
negativeClaims: CEP is not enterprise-ready or production-ready.
CEP is not proof of legal compliance, certification, market fit, HA, approved RTO/RPO, production scanner efficacy, production IdP effectiveness or independent assurance.
CEP does not allow a benchmark-only enterprise kernel to stand in for the canonical product runtime.
CEP does not allow SQLite/local process authorities to be described as distributed enterprise authorities.
CEP does not require microservices, Kafka, Redis, a full event store, an ORM or a managed SaaS control plane unless later evidence reopens them.
cepDefinition.mandatoryTruth: The enterprise product path and the local compatibility path may use different technical adapters, but they may not have different business semantics, claim boundaries, procedure identities, human-decision authority or receipt/evidence meaning.

abstractionLevels.name: product-and-claim
abstractionLevels.cepRequirement: Exactly seven peer business procedures; EP-01 cross-cutting only; AI proposal-only; repository green never equals deployment assurance.

abstractionLevels.name: operating-model
abstractionLevels.cepRequirement: Customer-controlled deployment remains a first-class target; distributed contributors, accountable function ownership and read-oriented assurance remain explicit.

abstractionLevels.name: business-capability
abstractionLevels.cepRequirement: RN-01, EC-01, AO-01, MC-01, AP-01, RC-01 and AR-01 retain native checkpoints, worklists, handoffs, verified closure and evidence semantics.

abstractionLevels.name: semantic-and-epistemic
abstractionLevels.cepRequirement: Observed/proposed/decided/attested, applicability/mapping/effectiveness, completion/verification and evidence/conclusion remain non-collapsible axes with versioned subject identity and explicit basis.

abstractionLevels.name: api-and-authorization
abstractionLevels.cepRequirement: One HTTP/business contract, role/scope/tenant authorization before mutation, same-as-read exports, bounded projections and stable error/receipt contracts.

abstractionLevels.name: application-runtime
abstractionLevels.cepRequirement: One Semantic Runtime Port owns business read/write semantics; local and enterprise adapters implement it without becoming parallel business authorities.

abstractionLevels.name: data-concurrency-and-work
abstractionLevels.cepRequirement: Enterprise mode uses shared durable authority, tenant isolation, subject-scoped OCC, command replay, bounded atomic receipts, incremental integrity, durable fenced work and revision-gap recovery.

abstractionLevels.name: objects-and-evidence
abstractionLevels.cepRequirement: Shared blob/object authority preserves quarantine/clean states, digest binding, scanner attestation and same-as-read evidence; byte storage never creates authenticity claims.

abstractionLevels.name: identity-security-and-privacy
abstractionLevels.cepRequirement: Enterprise identity is upstream-authenticated and fail-closed; tenant membership is server-side; secrets are external references; privacy retention/hold/erasure and abuse controls remain explicit.

abstractionLevels.name: ai-and-integrations
abstractionLevels.cepRequirement: OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek and custom-compatible adapters remain protocol-specific behind one AI boundary; provider/background work is durable async where appropriate; AI never becomes decision authority.

abstractionLevels.name: reliability-observability-and-recovery
abstractionLevels.cepRequirement: Stateless replicas, external telemetry port, health/integrity distinction, encrypted recovery points, migration/rollback policy and failure drills have explicit evidence classes.

abstractionLevels.name: delivery-and-governance
abstractionLevels.cepRequirement: Exact-head CI, dependency/provenance/SBOM/signing policy, branch/review governance, immutable release identity and deployment evidence envelopes are separated from product claims.

abstractionLevels.name: human-and-external-assurance
abstractionLevels.cepRequirement: E3-HUMAN, E3-GOV and E4-DEPLOY remain external rails; CEP requires their absence to remain visible rather than synthesized by repository tests.

concurrentSemanticMutations.shape: Keep current RuntimeStore/SQLite as canonical; add external TLS/IdP/scanner/backup controls.
concurrentSemanticMutations.reason: Improves deployment hygiene but leaves shared durable authority, cross-replica concurrency, durable distributed work and stateless replica semantics absent; the repository itself classifies RuntimeStore as scale-blocked.

concurrentSemanticMutations.shape: One business/epistemic runtime contract; SQLite local adapter and PostgreSQL enterprise adapter implement the same semantic port.
concurrentSemanticMutations.reason: Preserves local simplicity while preventing two business truths and permits enterprise capabilities without rewriting product semantics.

concurrentSemanticMutations.shape: Replace the canonical local runtime entirely with PostgreSQL enterprise authority.
concurrentSemanticMutations.reason: Valid enterprise path, but mandatory removal of the bounded local mode is not required by current evidence and would increase install friction without semantic gain.

concurrentSemanticMutations.shape: Split procedures/services behind Kafka/Redis/service mesh with independent stores.
concurrentSemanticMutations.reason: Adds authority, consistency and operational complexity without a demonstrated product requirement; conflicts with one-authority-per-semantic-slot and current evidence does not require it.

concurrentSemanticMutations.shape: Rewrite state as a complete event store and reconstruct all projections exclusively from events.
concurrentSemanticMutations.reason: Current semantics already separate snapshot, audit, subject versions and epistemic steps; full reconstruction is not needed for CEP and would create a large migration/authority rewrite.

concurrentSemanticMutations.shape: Make cloud multi-tenant SaaS the primary topology with organization control plane and shared managed services.
concurrentSemanticMutations.reason: Contradicts the current customer-controlled primary topology and introduces product/operating-model scope beyond the bounded target.

concurrentSemanticMutations.shape: Stateless ICTC app replicas plus customer-controlled PostgreSQL, shared object storage, upstream identity, ingress and telemetry.
concurrentSemanticMutations.reason: Matches the product operating model, reuses the existing enterprise kernel and keeps external infrastructure as deployment authority.

concurrentSemanticMutations.shape: Embed OIDC/SAML session authority directly inside ICTC.
concurrentSemanticMutations.reason: Enterprise identity is required, but direct embedded identity is not; the existing trusted-header/Shibboleth boundary can remain the minimal application contract when upstream authentication is proven.

concurrentSemanticMutations.shape: Turn every write into queued work and return eventual receipts.
concurrentSemanticMutations.reason: Business mutations and human decisions require atomic accepted/rejected write truth and readback; only provider/background work benefits from durable async execution.

concurrentSemanticMutations.shape: Treat provenance, evidence envelopes, external controls and explicit evidence grades as first-class closure conditions around the runtime.
concurrentSemanticMutations.reason: Prevents repository/runtime evidence from being laundered into deployment, human or independent assurance and gives CEP a falsifiable claim boundary.

semanticInvariants: one canonical business/epistemic contract across runtime modes
exactly seven business procedures and EP-01 cross-cutting
human authority preserved at decision checkpoints
subject identity/version and command identity are persistence-independent
enterprise mode is mounted by the real product server path, not only a benchmark server
enterprise mode uses PostgreSQL shared durable authority with RLS and subject-scoped OCC
local SQLite mode remains explicitly local/compatibility and cannot satisfy enterprise-scale posture
durable provider/background work is asynchronous; ordinary accepted business mutations retain atomic receipt semantics
shared blob/quarantine/scanner semantics are adapter-backed and same-as-read
identity, distributed rate authority, telemetry, key custody and scanner efficacy remain deployment-bound where appropriate
exact-head repository evidence and external E3/E4 evidence remain distinct
technology is admitted only when it closes a named invariant or evidence gap

minimumTechnologySupplyChain.repoOwned: sink port/correlation yes; collector operations external

minimumTechnologySupplyChain.minimum: Encrypted database/object backup with off-host target and restore drill
minimumTechnologySupplyChain.repoOwned: recovery primitive/verification yes; off-host durability and objectives external

minimumTechnologySupplyChain.minimum: Pinned build environment, dependency inventory/SBOM, signed artifact/provenance and exact-head verification

sliceLattice.purpose: Reconcile post-PR141/162 truth: release identity, capability truth, enterprise-candidate terminology, convergence state and exact current runtime facts without changing business behavior.
dod: market-candidate vs CEP vs enterprise-ready terms have non-overlapping definitions
enterprise bench kernel and canonical server mounts are separately declared

dod: current seven ProcedureAdapters bind to the port
local and enterprise adapters expose identical semantic capability IDs
whole-state draft mutation is not part of the enterprise contract

sliceLattice.purpose: Migrate handler writes from callback mutation of a whole Store draft to declarative subject-scoped command plans that preserve epistemic effects and cross-subject lineage.
dod: expected subject version replaces tenant-global revision as enterprise conflict authority
all seven procedures and 24 handoff predicates retain native invariants

sliceLattice.purpose: Bind Semantic Runtime Port to the existing PostgreSQL enterprise authority/kernel and close read/write parity against the local adapter.
dod: no process-local business authority in enterprise mode

sliceLattice.purpose: Mount a shared blob authority for attachments/evidence while preserving quarantine, digest, scanner attestation, tenant isolation and erasure semantics.
dod: quarantine cannot be read as clean
erasure/legal-hold semantics span metadata and shared bytes

sliceLattice.purpose: Close enterprise request identity and tenant selection over the canonical product server.
dod: upstream authentication required for networked enterprise mode
role mapping and deny rules deterministic
no header can grant tenant membership

sliceLattice.purpose: Move provider/background execution to durable fenced work while preserving current provider protocol, egress, budget, schema and proposal-only boundaries.
dod: provider request accepted as durable queued work when async
retry/replay cannot duplicate committed business effect
manual path remains available where product contract requires it

sliceLattice.purpose: Bind distributed ingress decisions, external telemetry, health/integrity/SLO semantics and enterprise backup/restore evidence to one deployment identity.
dod: restore verifies tenant revision/audit/state root/object manifest

sliceLattice.purpose: Make the ordinary ICTC bootstrap/server able to select enterprise mode and execute the real Home/procedure/Admin/Evidence/API journeys against the enterprise adapter; the bench server becomes test tooling rather than a separate product runtime.
dod: npm/launcher enterprise profile reaches canonical server
13 canonical UI surfaces consume enterprise-backed projections
no benchmark-only endpoint is required by the UI
local mode remains explicit compatibility/development profile

sliceLattice.purpose: Close C2-class delivery provenance without turning repository mechanics into deployment certification.
dod: exact-head required check policy and review-governance evidence explicitly classified

sliceLattice.purpose: Issue a bounded CEP receipt only when the enterprise product path is canonical-mountable and all repository-owned CEP invariants are exact-head green.
dod: canonical enterprise product E2E green on PostgreSQL/shared authorities
1000-client benchmark remains benchmark evidence, not production capacity
all residual external E3/E4 rails listed as unresolved or externally evidenced
CEP receipt is stale on semantic input or dependency receipt drift

criticalFalsifiers: Any enterprise-mode business write still depends on Store.mutate whole-state draft semantics after R2.
Canonical server.mjs cannot mount the enterprise adapter without using the separate bench API.
A local/process-only authority is accepted as evidence for a distributed enterprise invariant.
SQLite and PostgreSQL modes produce different business/epistemic outcomes for the same command sequence.
Tenant membership can be granted by request-controlled input rather than server-side identity context.
A provider result can become decided/verified without authorized human action.
A clean attachment/evidence object can be served without the required trust transition.
A replica loss can erase an acknowledged enterprise business mutation or produce a duplicate committed effect.
CEP can become green while canonical enterprise product E2E is unexecuted.
CEP can become enterprise-ready solely from repository/CI evidence.
claimBoundary: This proposal is a design/falsification artifact only. It does not modify current ICTC authority, runtime, convergence planning or release maturity. Adoption requires an explicit authority/convergence decision and subsequent executable slices.
